quote: Do you know about how much an average PGE bills are? And I I honestly don't know.
stewart_read: The rep asks for the bill amount but David has no number on hand ('out of sight, out of mind'). The rep says 'No, I understand' and moves straight to the next verify item without probing further or looping back to the wife's high-thermostat-use comment from earlier to build urgency.

coaching_implication: When the customer can't produce a number, the rep should reach for the emotional anchor already on the table — David mentioned the thermostat running high because of his wife's health. Tying that back ('given how much that furnace runs with your wife home more, this bill's probably adding up') would have created the flip verbally even without a hard number.

coaching_implication: The rep handled scope correctly by not over-explaining, but should have explicitly bridged to the closer ('the specialist can walk through exactly how that plays into your options') rather than leaving David's question hanging on a soft 'that's kinda how we base the designs.'
